title: USRAP suspended 120 days; Syrian refugees barred; FY2017 capped at 50,000
summary: Suspended the refugee program for 120 days, suspended entry of Syrian refugees indefinitely, and capped FY2017 refugee entries at 50,000. Revoked and replaced by EO 13780, effective March 16, 2017.
refugee_effect: Direct: suspends refugee admissions and bars Syrian nationals as refugees.
source: Executive Order 13769: Protecting the Nation From Foreign Terrorist Entry Into the United States (82 FR 8977)

title: USRAP suspended 120 days; FY2017 capped at 50,000
summary: Replaced EO 13769: suspended refugee travel and decisions on refugee applications for 120 days and again capped FY2017 refugee entries at 50,000. The indefinite bar on Syrian refugees was not carried over. The 120-day period expired on October 24, 2017 (EO 13815).
refugee_effect: Direct: suspends refugee admissions worldwide for 120 days.
source: Executive Order 13780: Protecting the Nation From Foreign Terrorist Entry Into the United States (82 FR 13209)

title: USRAP resumed with enhanced vetting
summary: Ended the 120-day suspension and let refugee travel and adjudications resume with the additional screening procedures. Revoked by EO 14013 on February 4, 2021.
source: Executive Order 13815: Resuming the United States Refugee Admissions Program With Enhanced Vetting Capabilities (82 FR 50055)

title: FY2021: refugees from Somalia, Syria and Yemen barred
summary: The FY2021 determination barred refugees from Somalia, Syria and Yemen except religious-persecution cases, embassy referrals and family-reunification cases. PD 2021-05 (April 16, 2021) superseded it.
refugee_effect: Direct: excludes nationals of three countries from refugee admission.
source: Presidential Determination on Refugee Admissions for Fiscal Year 2021 (85 FR 71219)

title: Program rebuilt; EO 13815 revoked
summary: Directed agencies to rebuild and expand the refugee program and revoked EO 13815 and EO 13888. Revoked by EO 14163 on January 20, 2025.
refugee_effect: Direct: program policy; no country restriction.
source: Executive Order 14013: Rebuilding and Enhancing Programs To Resettle Refugees and Planning for the Impact of Climate Change on Migration (86 FR 8839)

title: Refugee entry suspended
summary: Suspended entry of refugees under USRAP, and DHS decisions on refugee applications, until a finding that resumption is in U.S. interests, except case-by-case admissions jointly approved by the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security. Still cited as in force by the FY2027 determination (Sept 25, 2026). Court challenges to the suspension are not tracked here.
refugee_effect: Direct: suspends refugee admissions worldwide; admissions since then are case-by-case exceptions (overwhelmingly Afrikaners under EO 14204).
source: Executive Order 14163: Realigning the United States Refugee Admissions Program (90 FR 8459)

title: Afrikaners prioritized for resettlement
summary: Directed the government to prioritize humanitarian relief, including refugee admission and resettlement, for Afrikaners in South Africa. The FY2026 and FY2027 determinations allocate admissions primarily to Afrikaners under this order.
refugee_effect: Direct: the one group admitted in numbers during the 2025– suspension.
source: Executive Order 14204: Addressing Egregious Actions of the Republic of South Africa (90 FR 9497)

title: Entry restricted for nationals of 19 countries
summary: Fully suspended entry (immigrant and nonimmigrant) of nationals of 12 countries and partially suspended it for 7 more. It does not apply to refugees already admitted, and says nothing in it limits seeking refugee status; the FY2026 determination nonetheless makes refugee admissions subject to it. Proclamation 10998 continued and widened it from January 1, 2026.
refugee_effect: Indirect: a travel ban, not a refugee rule, but PD 2025-13 makes FY2026 refugee admissions subject to it.
source: Proclamation 10949: Restricting the Entry of Foreign Nationals To Protect the United States From Foreign Terrorists and Other National Security and Public Safety Threats (90 FR 24497)

title: Entry restrictions widened to 39 countries and Palestinian Authority documents
summary: Kept the 12 full and 4 of the partial suspensions of Proclamation 10949, moved Laos and Sierra Leone to full, fully suspended 5 more countries (Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger, South Sudan, Syria) and travel on Palestinian Authority documents, partially suspended 15 more, and narrowed Turkmenistan to immigrants. Refugees already admitted are exempt. The FY2026 emergency determination and the FY2027 determination make refugee admissions subject to it.
refugee_effect: Indirect: a travel ban, not a refugee rule, but PD 2026-14 and PD 2026-24 make refugee admissions subject to it.
source: Proclamation 10998: Restricting and Limiting the Entry of Foreign Nationals To Protect the Security of the United States (90 FR 59717)
